title: fix: separate legacy bridge traffic in dashboards and KPI
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Replaces #15277 and #15400 with a smaller version. There are two traffic groups. Legacy is the two legacy public API bridge keys: `raw-buzzard` (image) and `legacy-text…gpt-oss` (text). Everything else is every other key.

- A new Tinybird pipe, `generation_events_classified`, adds `traffic_group` (`legacy` / `everything_else`) in one place. It is keyed by exact key ID.
- `generation_usage_hourly` stores `traffic_group`. The Grafana usage dashboards get a header toggle: Everything else (default) / Legacy / Both.
- The KPI weekly endpoints (active users, usage, retention, health, segments, agent/MCP) exclude legacy.
- Users & Balances has no toggle because it mixes account and usage panels. Its usage panels always exclude legacy.
- Adding a group later means one more branch in the pipe and one more toggle option.

| Last 7 days (prod) | Requests | Users | Pollen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Everything else | 3.69M | 8,316 | 4,372 |
| Legacy | 4.79M | 1 | 422 |

**Verified:** observability tests and build pass. Tinybird is deployed and live on **staging**: both groups are populated and `weekly_active_users` responds.

**Rollout:** deploy Tinybird to prod before merging, because the dashboards read `traffic_group`. The hourly table is backfilled from the materialized pipe.

gist.headline: The old bridge gets a lane
gist.blurb: The observability garden now labels the two legacy bridge keys before counting the flowers. Dashboards and weekly KPIs can look at modern traffic without one very busy old bridge doing interpretive statistics.
gist.summary: Added a Tinybird `generation_events_classified` pipe that labels exact-key traffic as `legacy` (`raw-buzzard` image and `legacy-text…gpt-oss` text) or `everything_else`, carries the field into `generation_usage_hourly`, and excludes legacy traffic from weekly KPI endpoints.
gist.impact: Grafana usage dashboards can switch between Everything else, Legacy, and Both, while weekly active-user, usage, retention, health, segments, and agent/MCP metrics consistently report non-legacy traffic by default.
